item.title: Money Fellows took an old savings habit and built a business the hard way
item.dc:creator: Adonijah Ndege
item.description: Money Fellows built its model around digitising an old saving habit in Egypt.

item.title: Afreximbank’s fresh $118m creative bet needs open borders to pay off
item.dc:creator: Frank Eleanya
item.description: Afreximbank’s $118 million commitment to Nigeria’s creative economy could help businesses scale, but access to finance alone will not unlock Africa’s creative potential. Cross-border trade barriers, weak intellectual property protection and limited routes to market remain major obstacles.

item.title: African firms pay 1.8% more for credit than their rich-country peers, IFC study shows
item.dc:creator: Godfrey George
item.description: African businesses pay significantly more to borrow in corporate bond markets than their counterparts in high-income economies, with firms on the continent facing a median real borrowing cost that is 180 basis points (1.8%) higher, according to research by the International Finance Corporation (IFC).

item.title: MTN’s South African data boom is not translating into revenue growth
item.dc:creator: Phathisani Moyo
item.description: MTN South Africa’s customers are consuming more mobile data than ever, but the country’s second-largest mobile operator is finding it difficult to translate that demand into revenue growth.

item.title: Nigeria could collect $75 million from crypto stamp duty in 2027
item.dc:creator: Temitayo Jaiyeola
item.description: Nigeria’s crypto market received $38.1 billion in value between July 2025 and June 2026, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, highlighting the scale of a market the government hopes to tap to expand its tax base in 2027.
